audience.text: Python developers who need to programmatically create, inspect, and convert 3D scene data without native dependencies.

capabilities.text: Construct hierarchical scene graphs using Scene, Node, Mesh, Camera, and Light objects.
capabilities.title: Build 3D scenes programmatically

capabilities.text: Import OBJ (with .mtl materials), STL (binary and ASCII), glTF 2.0 / GLB, COLLADA (.dae), and 3MF files into a common Scene model.
capabilities.title: Import multiple 3D formats

capabilities.text: Export Scene objects to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, and 3MF using Scene.save() with appropriate save options.
capabilities.title: Export to common 3D formats

capabilities.text: Assign PbrMaterial and other material types to nodes with properties like albedo, metallic_factor, and roughness_factor.
capabilities.title: Assign materials to scene entities

capabilities.text: Use Vector2/3/4, Matrix4, Quaternion, and BoundingBox types for transforms and spatial queries.
capabilities.title: Work with math utilities

capabilities.text: Define animations using AnimationClip, KeyframeSequence, KeyFrame, and AnimationNode to bind keyframes to node or material properties.
capabilities.title: Support animation with keyframes

limitations.text: COLLADA export is not reachable through the public Scene.save() API; the exporter dispatcher raises NotImplementedError before the Collada exporter is invoked.
FBX export via FbxExporter.save() and FbxExporter.save_to_stream() raises NotImplementedError; FBX support is experimental and not covered by full round-trip tests.
Mesh boolean operations (union, difference, intersect) and NURBS evaluation raise NotImplementedError.
The aspose.threed.render module (Renderer, IRenderWindow, etc.) is not implemented; this library does not render or rasterize scenes.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic construction and manipulation of 3D scene graphs using high-level Python objects like Scene, Node, Mesh, and primitives.
Supports round-trip import and export of common 3D formats—OBJ, STL, glTF, COLLADA, and 3MF—without requiring external native libraries.
Provides built-in parametric primitives (Box, Cylinder, Sphere, etc.) that can be converted to triangulated meshes for further processing.
Supports PBR and legacy material assignment (Lambert, Phong) with glTF-compatible properties for realistic rendering workflows.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, open-source library for building, importing, and exporting 3D scenes using an Aspose.3D-compatible API.

uncertainties: Whether COLLADA import fully supports all material and texture features beyond what the examples demonstrate.
Whether the Scene.from_file() method behaves identically to Scene.open() for all supported formats.
Whether the Scene.animation_clips property is populated automatically during import or only when explicitly created.
Whether the Scene.clear() method resets animation clips or only the scene graph nodes.

workflows.name: Create a mesh from control points and export to STL
workflows.text: Construct a Mesh by adding Vector4 control points and polygons, attach it to a Node in a Scene, and save to STL using FileFormat.get_format_by_extension and StlSaveOptions.

workflows.name: Assign PBR material and export to glTF
workflows.text: Create a Mesh, assign a PbrMaterial with albedo, metallic_factor, and roughness_factor to a Node, and save to glTF using GltfSaveOptions with explicit FileFormat.

workflows.name: Convert a primitive to a mesh
workflows.text: Instantiate a Box, Cylinder, Sphere, or other primitive and call to_mesh() to obtain a triangulated Mesh.

workflows.name: Build a cube and export to 3MF
workflows.text: Manually construct a cube mesh with 8 control points and 12 polygons, attach it to a Node, and save using ThreeMfSaveOptions.

workflows.name: Inspect or convert loaded scenes
workflows.text: Load OBJ, STL, glTF, COLLADA, or 3MF files using Scene.open() and inspect or modify the resulting node graph before saving to another format.
